name: Kenwal Steel - Tennessee
old_description: For decades, Kenwal has been a trusted leader in high-quality, precision flat-rolled steel solutions, delivering superior products and service to industries worldwide.
about:
Kenwal Steel operates a steel service center in Lebanon, Tennessee, part of a network that has processed flat-rolled steel for over 70 years. The company is led by Chairman and CEO Stephen Eisenberg, who describes the business as a critical part of manufacturing across the nation. Corporate headquarters are in Dearborn, Michigan, where the company also runs a pickling line.

The Tennessee location provides precision processing including pickling, slitting, tension leveling, packaging, and technical support. Kenwal runs seven slitting lines across its facilities and handles hot-rolled, cold-rolled, coated, and advanced high-strength steel (AHSS) grades. Its quality and environmental management systems are certified to IATF 16949 across all processing and distribution sites.

Customers span automotive, appliance, agriculture, construction, heavy equipment, industrial manufacturing, tubing, electronics, and energy generation. The company positions itself as a supplier that delivers the right grade of steel with quick turnaround from strategically placed service centers available 24/7.

Kenwal emphasizes integrity and long-term partnerships, built on decades of steel experience. Its differentiators include the pickling line in Dearborn, the multi-line slitting capacity, and a certified quality system that aims for right-first-time results.

name: Kiesub Electronics
about:
Kiesub Electronics was founded in 1973 in Las Vegas, Nevada, and has operated continuously from the same industrial center near the Strip. The company began as a wholesale electronics distributor serving the local market and has since expanded its footprint to an 11,000‑square‑foot facility that combines a walk‑in retail store with a manufacturing operation.

Today Kiesub functions as both a broad‑line distributor and a contract manufacturer. The distribution side stocks more than 75,000 electronic parts, components, and accessories, including one of the Southwest’s largest battery inventories. The contract manufacturing division, launched in 1995, produces custom cables, wire harnesses, printed circuit boards, and LED illumination products such as edge‑lit panels and signage for casinos, hotels, and entertainment venues. As a member of the Genie Group purchasing cooperative, Kiesub leverages the buying power of over 90 distributors and 300 locations to source from more than 300 manufacturer accounts.

The customer base spans gaming, entertainment, and hospitality businesses, as well as manufacturers, repair shops, low‑voltage contractors, utilities, school districts, universities, government agencies, and military installations. Hobbyists and walk‑in consumers are also served through the retail counter.

Kiesub emphasizes in‑house design and manufacturing to control quality, and it offers same‑day shipping on in‑stock orders placed before noon Pacific time. The company cites its experienced staff—many with 25‑plus years in the industry—and its Genie Group affiliation as key differentiators.

name: Kilo Hollow Energy
old_description: of your energy with custom-designed solar and battery systems.
about:
Kilo Hollow Energy operates from Ashland, Virginia, serving customers across Virginia, Maryland, Pennsylvania, and Washington, D.C. The company is led by President William Branch and is described as a family-owned business. Founded to provide custom-designed solar and battery systems, the firm focuses on residential and commercial energy independence.

The company designs and installs solar photovoltaic arrays, battery storage systems, and provides electrical service upgrades including 200A and 400A panel changes, EV charger circuits, and generator installations. Its in-house team handles design, permitting, installation, and ongoing maintenance for projects ranging from 4.8 kW residential rooftops to 1 MW commercial arrays. Services also include diagnostics, inverter monitoring, thermal imaging, and system removal or relocation.

Kilo Hollow serves homeowners, businesses, and off-grid clients seeking whole-home backup, grid independence, or reduced utility costs. Commercial customers include property owners looking to offset carbon emissions and enhance market appeal. The firm navigates local codes across its four-state service area and coordinates with utilities for interconnection.

As a Tesla Energy Certified Installer, the company emphasizes premium components and craftsmanship, offering complete service from initial design through long-term maintenance. Its differentiators include a fully in-house workforce, family-owned customer approach, and expertise in both roof-mounted and ground-mount configurations tailored to each site.

name: Kimray Manufacturing Services
old_description: Our products are engineered, sourced, manufactured, and supported by our expert teams to make sure they work for you.
about:
Kimray Manufacturing Services, operating as Kimray, Inc., is headquartered in Oklahoma City, Oklahoma. The company designs and manufactures a broad line of oil and gas control equipment, including valves, regulators, controllers, pumps, actuators, and related accessories. The founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, but the business emphasizes its American-made production and a culture known as the Kimray Way.

Kimray’s operations span engineering, sourcing, manufacturing, and post-sale support, all performed in-house. The company maintains ten company-owned stores across the United States and a network of authorized distributors worldwide, shipping products directly from those locations. Beyond hardware, Kimray provides store services, field maintenance, project consultations, and product training—both hands-on and self-paced online. A dedicated platform, Kimray Electrix™, bundles electric actuation, emissions-reduction tools, and expertise to help operators lower methane output and improve site control.

The primary customers are oil and gas producers, from large international energy companies to independent operators. The company states that “top energy producers in the world use Kimray” and its equipment is found on well sites, production vessels, and gas-processing facilities. Applications include liquid dumping, pressure regulation, level control, glycol pumping, and emissions compliance.

Kimray differentiates itself through the Kimray Way—a stated belief in people, a mission to make a difference, unwavering values, and a promise to customers. The company says it does not simply run machines, assemble parts, or ship products; rather, its team works toward common goals to ensure customers get the most out of each product. This philosophy, combined with a Made-in-USA commitment, underpins its positioning as a premium partner.

Kin Ship Goods operates from a storefront in Charleston, West Virginia. The company's founding year and ownership structure are not publicly disclosed, nor are the names of its founders.

The business runs both a physical shop and an e-commerce site, offering a mix of apparel (short-sleeve tees, crop tees, long-sleeve tees, sweatshirts), accessories (hats, totes, beanies, stickers, mugs, prints, koozies, keychains, pins), and a curated selection of books, journals, bags, jewelry, socks, home goods, food items, miniatures, children's products, and pet accessories. A "MADE BY US" line suggests some products are designed or produced in-house, while collaborations with artists such as Patti Smith and Jeff Buckley add exclusive items. No details on manufacturing processes, facility size, headcount, or production volumes are provided.

Kin Ship Goods serves primarily retail consumers, including tourists and locals seeking West Virginia-themed merchandise, gift items, and artist collaborations. The shop is open Tuesday through Saturday 10 a.m.–6 p.m. and Sunday 10 a.m.–2 p.m. There is no indication of B2B or wholesale operations.

The company has not publicly stated a founding mission or specific differentiators beyond its curated product mix and local presence.

name: Kingston Krafts
old_description: Custom length, width, height and top thickness available on most products.
about:
Kingston Krafts operates from Cranston, Rhode Island, as a family-owned and operated small business. The company specializes in custom metal and wood furniture and fixtures, drawing on the region’s industrial heritage.

The workshop fabricates bar tops, countertops, dining tables, and custom furniture using zinc, copper, brass, bronze, and solid wood. Customers can specify custom length, width, height, and top thickness on most products, and choose from standard finishes or custom patinas. An in-house design team provides expert advice, and the company ships nationwide with free shipping; installation services are available in the Northeast and Southeast United States.

Kingston Krafts serves both commercial and residential clients. Its portfolio ranges from small cafes to large casinos, supplying metal and wood surfaces for hospitality and home environments.

The founders frame their ethos around the legacy of the American Industrial Revolution, aiming to build beautiful, well-designed products that last a lifetime. They emphasize the challenge of custom work and pride in their standard collections, positioning the business as part of Rhode Island’s creative revival.

name: Kinsman Separation Service, LLC
old_description: Service Site Visits, Start Up Services, PM Maintenance Programs, Used Equipment Sales
about:
Kinsman Separation Service, LLC operates from Stillwater, Minnesota. The company was founded by Scott Fortune, a material processing consultant with over ten years of hands-on experience in separation systems. Fortune established the business to help processing facilities improve efficiency, reduce downtime, and optimize separation equipment performance.

The firm provides nationwide consulting and field services for separation and processing equipment. Its offerings include equipment inspection, processing system audits, startup services, preventative maintenance programs, new and used equipment sales, and equipment repair. The company specializes in Forsberg separation equipment and works with a range of brands from manufacturers such as Bühler Group, Cimbria, AGI, Carter Day International, Oliver Manufacturing, Westrup, SWECO, Rotex Global, Kason Corporation, General Kinematics, Donaldson Torit, and Kice.

Kinsman serves processing facilities across the United States that rely on separation, screening, vibratory, and material handling systems. Typical customers include grain, seed, and agricultural processing plants that use equipment from the brands listed above. The company's partners list reflects the equipment ecosystems it supports.

Fortune started the business to bring specialized, hands-on expertise directly to plant operators, offering a single point of contact for inspection, maintenance, and equipment procurement to keep separation lines running reliably.

about:
Klock Werks operates from Mitchell, South Dakota. The company's founding year is not publicly stated, though a copyright notice spans 1997–2026. Ownership structure and founder names have not been disclosed.

The company designs and manufactures a range of motorcycle parts and accessories. Its signature product is the Flare® Windshield, a patented windshield design for touring motorcycles. The lineup also includes iOmounts® magnetic device mounts for motorcycles, cars, trucks, and heavy equipment; fenders, fairings, handlebars, and hardware; and a trio of cleaning lines—Shine Werks, Matte Werks, and Engine Werks—along with Dynamat® sound-damping material. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are published.

Klock Werks serves the powersports aftermarket, supplying riders and dealers with parts for Harley-Davidson®, Indian®, BMW®, Honda®, Kawasaki®, Yamaha®, Victory®, and Polaris®/Slingshot® models. The magnetic mounts are also marketed for automotive, agricultural, UTV/ATV, marine, and industrial applications. A dealer program supports retail distribution.

The business traces its identity to the development of the Flare® Windshield, which the company presents as an original solution for wind management on bagger-style motorcycles. The iOmounts® system is promoted as a secure, versatile mounting platform. No further statements on founding mission or competitive differentiation are provided in the source material.
